method: REA 6.10.1 with Ghidra 12.2, static analysis only
observed: Client accepts a command and optional device path, default /dev/smd11.
Writes the supplied command followed by CRLF; reads and prints lines until a terminal reply.
The recovered command path uses blocking reads, not an internal QSCAN progress or SIM-disable workflow.
The shell gatekeeper provides serialization, an AT warm-up and a 300-second outer safety cap.
The RM520N native broker source explicitly uses a 300-second long-command deadline and timeout resynchronization.
limitations: Ghidra reports control-flow warnings in the stripped Rust executable; findings describe the recovered normal command path, not a complete reconstruction.
The old 180-second deadline cut off replies at the measured completion boundary. Successful validation included a warm-up and a longer deadline; their individual effects were not isolated.
SIM fallback polling was observed on the USB AT port during an MHI scan. The updated SIM daemon pauses all its AT paths while a validated scanner worker owns the modem.
Percentages are estimates capped below 100 until successful completion.
No third-party executable or decompiled implementation is included in the firmware.
